main_result: Conditional on the cited companion theorem (Theorem thm:input: a finite field K_2 of characteristic two, a finitely generated H_2, and a_2, b_2 in K_2[H_2] with a_2b_2=1 but b_2a_2 != 1), the manuscript builds a finitely generated group G_D = (direct sum of C_3 indexed by H_2) semidirect H_2 and an integer matrix A of size 2d+1 over Z[G_D] (d = [K_2:F_2]) that is invertible over Q[G_D]. Its Fuglede-Kadison determinant is q^{-theta} with q = 2^k, q ≡ 1 mod 3^{1+|S|}, and theta = (1/3)(2/3)^{|S|} > 0. So 0 < det < 1, and the integral of log t against the spectral measure is finite and negative. This contradicts the square, unrestricted group-ring Determinant Conjecture as the manuscript states it.
proof_strategy: Lemma binary turns a_2, b_2 into d x d matrices X, Y over F_2[H_2] with XY = I and an idempotent defect C = I - YX with XC = 0 and CY = 0; I checked these identities. Proposition separation builds a rational projection p = p_1 prod_{s in S}(1 - p_s) on the C_3-part, using commuting averaging idempotents, so that psp = 0 for s in S; its identity coefficient is theta. Reducing mod 2 and sandwiching the normalized defect entry gives a factorization of diag(I_d, p-bar) through d columns. Lemma lift lifts that factorization to Z/2^k using a finite geometric series, and Lemma integral builds the integral block matrix A = M(1) from a path M(x) = L_x B R_x with B = diag(qI_r, J); I checked the block products, the inverse of J, and the integrality. Lemmas trace, logderivative and shears show that the unipotent shears leave tau(log M*M) unchanged, so log det A = log det B = (r - tau_m(P)) log q, and I checked this derivative computation step by step. The trace of B*B gives (r - tau_m(P)) log q, which yields the value -theta log q.
hardest_part: I could check the internal algebra (the idempotent and separation identities, the trace coefficient [1]p = theta, the block product, the shear derivative and the log-derivative formula) line by line and found no error. What I cannot verify is the external input (Theorem thm:input), and whether the manuscript's conjecture (eq:conjecture) matches the literature formulation of Luck's Conjecture 13.2, including any torsion or injectivity hypotheses. Those determine whether the claimed refutation is valid, and the manuscript does not reproduce the wording.

main_result: Conditional on Theorem 1.1 of the companion paper (a finite-characteristic-two group algebra K_2[H_2] that is not directly finite), the manuscript constructs a finitely generated group G_D = (⊕_{h∈H_2} C_3) ⋊ H_2 and a square integer matrix A over Z[G_D] (size 2d+1, where d = [K_2:F_2]) that is invertible over Q[G_D]. Its Fuglede–Kadison determinant is q^{-θ} with θ = (1/3)(2/3)^{|S|} > 0 and q a power of 2 with q ≡ 1 mod 3^{1+|S|}. So 0 < det < 1, and the logarithmic integral of the spectral measure is finite and negative. This refutes the square-matrix instance of the group-ring Determinant Conjecture (the lower bound det ≥ 1).
proof_strategy: Lemma binary turns the field-level pair a_2b_2=1≠b_2a_2 into matrices X,Y over F_2[H_2] with XY=I and an idempotent defect C=I−YX≠0 satisfying XC=0, CY=0. Proposition separation builds a rational projection p in Q[⊕C_3] by multiplying p_1 by commuting factors (1−p_s), so that psp=0 for s∈S kills all but the identity term modulo 2; this gives τ(p)=θ and a mod-2 factorization of diag(I,p) through d columns. Lemma lift lifts that factorization to Z/qZ by a geometric series in the nilpotent 2-divisible part, and Lemma integral builds an integral block matrix A = M(1) from block shears of B = diag(qI_r, J). Lemmas logderivative and shears show the log-trace is invariant along the shear path, so τ(log A*A) equals τ(log B*B) = 2(r−τ_m(P)) log q. Substituting r=d and τ_{d+1}(P)=d+θ gives the claimed determinant. I checked each algebraic identity (C²=C, the block products, the inverse of J, the derivative formula, the trace identities, psp=0, the coefficient θ) by hand and found them consistent; the only inputs I could not check are the cited theorems.
hardest_part: The cited input, Theorem 1.1 of the companion paper (existence of a non-directly-finite group algebra over a finite characteristic-two field). Everything downstream depends on it, and I cannot verify it from the manuscript. Of the checked material, the analytic shear-invariance argument (Lemma logderivative, the Ω-series and termwise differentiation, then Lemma shears) was the most intricate, and I verified it by hand, but I would still want an independent check of the uniform-convergence bookkeeping.

main_result: Given a finitely generated group H_2 and a finite field K_2 of characteristic two with a_2b_2=1 but b_2a_2≠1 (the cited input), the manuscript builds a finitely generated group G_D = (⊕_{h∈H_2} C_3) ⋊ H_2 and an integer square matrix A over Z[G_D], invertible over Q[G_D], whose Fuglede–Kadison-type determinant (unnormalized-trace convention) equals q^{-θ} with q a power of 2 (q ≡ 1 mod D), θ = (1/3)(2/3)^{|S|} > 0, so 0 < det < 1. The integral ∫ log t dμ_A is finite and equals -2θ log q/(2d+1) < 0. This contradicts the unrestricted square-matrix group-ring Determinant Conjecture (det ≥ 1 for nonsingular integer matrices). The result is conditional on the cited non-direct-finiteness theorem.
proof_strategy: Lemma binary turns the non-directly-finite pair a_2,b_2 over K_2 into X,Y ∈ Mat_d(F_2[H_2]) with XY=I, YX≠I, and the defect C=I−YX is an idempotent with XC=0, CY=0. Proposition separation builds, inside G_D, a rational projection p = p_1∏_{s∈S}(1−p_s) built from commuting 3-cycle averagers, with psp=0 for s∈S, so that after reduction mod 2 the sandwich p̄ h_0^{-1}C_ij p̄ collapses to p̄, giving P̄ = uv through d columns while τ(P)=d+θ. Lemma lift lifts the factorization modulo q=2^k by a finite geometric series, and Lemma integral builds an integral A = L_1 B R_1 from block shears and B = diag(qI_r, J). Lemmas logderivative and shears show that shears do not change τ(log(M*M)) because the derivative is 2Re τ(M'M^{-1}) and the diagonal blocks of M'M^{-1} vanish. Evaluating at B gives τ(log(B*B)) = 2(r−τ(P)) log q, and substituting r=d, τ=d+θ gives the determinant. I re-derived the block products, the idempotent and trace identities, the psp=0 argument, the mod-2 sandwich, the factorization uv, the lifting, and the shear derivative formula, and found them consistent; the unverified dependence is the cited input and the external sofic remark.
hardest_part: The argument's truth rests on Theorem input (non-direct-finiteness of K_2[H_2]), which the manuscript itself says is not proved or tested here; I could not check it, and nothing in the rest of the chain can compensate if it fails. Within the manuscript, the step I would least trust myself to have checked independently is the normal-form argument in Proposition separation Step 4 (identity coefficient of the product of mixed-label factors), together with the block-trace bookkeeping in Lemma shears, though on reading both appeared correct.
